title: LDO dissipation including ground current
description: Calculate electrical heat in an enabled single-supply LDO from pass-path and operating ground-current losses.
formula: Ppass = (Vin-Vout) Iout; Pgnd = Vin Ignd; Pdiss = Ppass+Pgnd
assumptions: Enabled single-input-rail LDO in regulation; use ground current at the actual load, voltage and temperature, not necessarily no-load IQ.
Input headroom must meet the entered operating-point dropout requirement. Check device current/voltage ratings and thermal viability separately.
Separate bias supplies, reverse current, shutdown and external divider losses are excluded. Electrical heat power is not junction temperature.

references.title: TI SLYY206, Understanding the Foundations of Quiescent Current in Linear Power Systems, equation 1 and dropout discussion

inputs.label: Required dropout headroom at this load

constraints.message: Input-output headroom must meet the operating-point dropout requirement.

title: Boost output capacitor with ESR budget
description: Size effective boost output capacitance for the switch-on load-supply gap and full output-path ESR current step.
formula: D = (Vout-Vin)/Vout; ILpeak = Iout Vout/Vin+delta_I/2; Vesr_pp = ESR ILpeak; Cmin = Iout D/[fs (Vbudget_pp-Vesr_pp)]
assumptions: Ideal single-phase fixed-frequency boost with triangular CCM current, constant load, small output ripple, constant ESR and negligible ESL.
Valley inductor current must be at least load current for monotonic off-interval capacitor charging; this is stronger than CCM.
ESR ripple uses the full peak rectifier-path current step, not just inductor ripple. Summed ESR/capacitive excursions are a conservative bound.
Use effective capacitance; compensation, load steps, derating and current ratings require separate checks. The 10% output-ripple ceiling is a catalog small-ripple guard.

references.title: TI SLVA372D, Basic Calculation of a Boost Converter's Power Stage, section 7 equations 12 and 13
TI SLVAFJ5, boost current topology and ideal duty

outputs.label: Peak output-path current during off interval

constraints.message: Boost operation requires output voltage above input voltage.
Inductor valley must be at least load current for monotonic off-interval capacitor charging.
ESR ripple must leave a positive capacitive ripple budget.
This small-ripple model accepts ripple budgets at most 10% of output voltage.

title: Buck input capacitor RMS current
description: Calculate total RMS ripple current in a buck input capacitor bank, including triangular inductor ripple.
formula: D = Vout/Vin; ICin_rms = hypot(Iout sqrt(D (Vin-Vout)/Vin), delta_I sqrt(D/12))
assumptions: Ideal single-phase fixed-frequency buck in CCM with triangular ripple and approximately constant voltages.
Source supplies only DC average current; the local input capacitor bank supplies all switching-frequency AC current.
Result is for the total bank, not individual parallel capacitors. ESR/ESL, source impedance, interleaving and layout change sharing.

references.title: TI SSZTBI6, Power Tips: How to Select Ceramic Capacitors to Meet Ripple-Current Requirements, equation 2

outputs.label: Total input capacitor RMS ripple current

constraints.message: Buck operation requires input voltage above output voltage.
Positive inductor valley current is required for the CCM model.

title: Boost right-half-plane zero
description: Estimate the boost CCM duty-to-output right-half-plane zero and conservative one-tenth-frequency crossover guideline.
formula: D = (Vout-Vin)/Vout; Rload = Vout/Iout; fRHPZ = (Vin/Iout) (Vin/Vout)/(2 pi L); fc_guideline = fRHPZ/10
assumptions: Ideal single-phase boost averaged small-signal power stage in CCM with resistive incremental load Rload=Vout/Iout.
Fixed-frequency PWM, small perturbations, negligible winding resistance and semiconductor drops. Constant-power loads, DCM, interleaving and strongly nonlinear operation invalidate the model.
Positive valley current is enforced from ideal triangular switching ripple.
One-tenth RHP-zero frequency is the conservative end of TI's one-fifth-to-one-tenth guideline, not a stability guarantee. Full loop analysis and switching-frequency separation remain necessary.

references.title: TI SLVAFJ5, How to Approach a Power-Supply Design Part 3, boost equation 7 and bandwidth limitation
TI SLVA372D, boost inductor ripple equation 2

outputs.label: Conservative crossover guideline, not stability certification

constraints.message: Boost operation requires output voltage above input voltage.
Inductor average current must exceed half the ideal ripple to remain in CCM.

title: Converter input current and loss budget
description: Budget DC source current and aggregate converter loss from output power and operating-point total efficiency.
formula: Pout = Vout Iout; Pin = Pout/eta; Iin = Pin/Vin; Ploss = Pout (1-eta)/eta = Pin-Pout
assumptions: Steady-state single-input, single-output DC converter with positive nonzero load and 0<total efficiency<=1.
Efficiency is total power efficiency at this operating point, including control/ground power; do not add those losses again.
Power-conservation budgeting, not topology voltage transfer or device-loss prediction. Startup, switching ripple, transients and multi-rail bias power are excluded.

references.title: TI SLYY206, power efficiency definition, equation 2
TI SLVA118A, Linear Regulator Design Guide For LDOs, section 3 conservation of energy equations 1-4

inputs.label: Total power efficiency as a fraction

title: Buck CCM inductor sizing
description: Size an ideal buck inductor for chosen peak-to-peak ripple fraction and calculate current endpoints.
formula: D = Vout/Vin; delta_I = r Iout; Lmin = (Vin-Vout) D/(fs delta_I); Ipeak,valley = Iout (1 +/- r/2)
assumptions: Ideal fixed-frequency single-phase buck in steady-state CCM; switch drops and winding resistance are neglected.
Ripple ratio means peak-to-peak ripple divided by average output current; 0<r<2 guarantees positive valley at this load.
Lmin is effective inductance at operating bias. Tolerances, saturation rating and controller recommendations require separate checks. Duty is ideal, not efficiency-corrected.

references.title: TI SLVA057, Understanding Buck Power Stages in Switchmode Power Supplies, section 2.1
TI SLVA477, Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage, section 3

constraints.message: Buck operation requires input voltage above output voltage.

title: Boost CCM inductor sizing
description: Size an ideal boost inductor using ripple relative to average input-inductor current and calculate current stress.
formula: D = (Vout-Vin)/Vout; ILavg = Iout Vout/Vin; delta_I = r ILavg; Lmin = Vin D/(fs delta_I); Ipeak,valley = ILavg (1 +/- r/2)
assumptions: Ideal fixed-frequency single-phase boost in steady-state CCM; losses, switch drops and winding resistance are neglected.
Ripple ratio is relative to average input-inductor current, not output current; 0<r<2 guarantees positive valley.
Use effective inductance at operating current. Saturation, tolerance, control stability and actual current limits require separate checks.

references.title: TI SLVA372D, Basic Calculation of a Boost Converter's Power Stage, sections 2 and 3
TI SLVAFJ5, How to Approach a Power-Supply Design Part 3, ideal boost duty

constraints.message: Boost operation requires output voltage above input voltage.

title: Buck output capacitor with ESR budget
description: Allocate buck peak-to-peak output ripple between ESR and capacitor charge, then size effective capacitance.
formula: Vesr_pp = ESR delta_I; Vcap_budget = Vbudget_pp-Vesr_pp; Cmin = delta_I/(8 fs Vcap_budget)
assumptions: Single-phase CCM buck with triangular inductor ripple and constant load; ESR is resistive at switching frequency and ESL is neglected.
The sum of capacitive and ESR peak-to-peak ripple is a conservative bound, not an assertion that extrema coincide.
The ripple budget is at most 10% of output voltage as an explicit catalog small-ripple guard.
Use effective capacitance after bias, temperature and tolerance derating. Controller stability and load steps can require more capacitance.

references.title: TI SLVA477, Basic Calculation of a Buck Converter's Power Stage, section 7 minimum output capacitance and ESR ripple equations

constraints.message: Positive inductor valley current is required for the CCM model.
